label: Now · Current Role
title: Taking AI Radiation Oncology Global
demoCaption: OncoStudio — AI auto-contouring of organs and tumors on CT/MR
lead: As Chief Business and Technology Officer, I lead Oncosoft's Global Business Division, taking an end-to-end AI platform for radiation oncology from regulatory clearance to clinical adoption across the US, Japan, Southeast Asia, and Latin America.

blocks.label: Problem
blocks.text: Radiation therapy planning still depends on manual contouring of organs and tumors: slow, variable between clinicians, and a bottleneck to treating more patients. For AI to fix that worldwide, it has to clear each market's regulators and reach clinics through channels they already trust.

blocks.label: Approach
blocks.text: OncoStudio auto-contours organs-at-risk and tumors, major organs in about a minute, inside existing PACS, TPS, and EMR workflows. It anchors a platform with OncoFlow (workflow), OncoPlan (particle-therapy planning), and OncoAgent, a guideline-aware AI agent published at MICCAI 2026. My division turns that platform into market access: country-by-country regulatory entry, distribution and industry partnerships, government R&D programs and IP, and clinical AI deployment engineers who support adoption on site.

blocks.label: Impact
blocks.text: Cleared in six countries (Korea, US FDA 510(k), Japan, Singapore, Brazil, Indonesia), distributed in Chile through exclusive distributor OPUS, and used in 20+ hospitals in Korea. Mayo Clinic Florida is a customer under a 2025 solution supply agreement and a clinical validation partner; GenXRT is our first US commercial partner; Anzai Medical is the exclusive distributor in Japan. In particle therapy, OncoPlan was cleared by the MFDS in 2026 as the first carbon-ion treatment planning system developed by a Korean company, with Yonsei Cancer Center as technology transfer and joint R&D partner for carbon-ion planning and Samsung Medical Center as joint R&D partner for proton therapy validation.

label: Flagship Career Impact · 2020–2023
title: AI Cloud Platform for 3D-Bioprinted Wound Regeneration
lead: An AI platform that turns a single tablet photo of a wound into a ready-to-print 3D patch model in seconds — then bio-prints it at the point of care to treat diabetic foot ulcers, deployed across the US, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America.

blocks.label: Problem
blocks.text: Personalized regenerative patches require precise scanning, CAD modeling, and bioprinting — work that a surgical team anywhere in the world cannot realistically do at the point of care. To reach patients globally, the hard part had to disappear into software.

blocks.label: Approach
blocks.text: We built an AI platform (AiD Regen) that, from a single tablet RGB-D photo, segments the wound, reconstructs its 3D surface, and generates a ready-to-print 3D model in about 30 seconds. Production-grade MLOps on Google Cloud (Vertex AI, GKE) delivers identical quality at any clinical site — no on-site AI specialist required.

blocks.label: Impact
blocks.text: Founded and scaled the AI department from zero to 15, achieved both FDA and CE clearance, and drove the full commercial cycle from MVP to $1B+ in long-term contracts across the US, India, Turkey, the Middle East, and Latin America. Launched on AWS in 6 months, then migrated to Google Cloud in 3 — the work became a featured Google Cloud customer story.
